news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /15Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
12Z update...no major changes to previous TAFs. Earlier
discussion below.

===========================================================

Today...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact timing.

IFR with localized LIFR. Higher terrain snow continues with a
cold rain elsewhere, which may be heavy at times. Do have some
uncertainty on visibilities as the GLAMP, MAV and MET seemed
much too low for all terminals based on most being under a plain
rain. Think the risk of lower visibilities is highest near the
low pressure center as winds become variable per past
experience. Winds out of the E to NE at 15-30 kts with gusts of
30-45 kts. The highest speeds/gusts will be found along the
coastal plain. Could have some embedded thunderstorms across the
Island terminals and perhaps this Cape this afternoon, but
confidence was not high enough to include in the latest TAF.

Tonight...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact timing.

IFR conditions gradually improving to MVFR across western MA/CT
and southern RI toward daybreak. Rain across eastern areas, but
changing over to snow in the lower elevations across the west as
precip is winding down and colder air filtering in. Winds start
off NE at 10-20 kts shifting to the N/NW late. Gusts of 25-35
kts.

Saturday...High confidence.

Precipitation coming to an end for most by late morning. MVFR
conditions persisting for most of the day, but could see fairly
widespread VFR by late afternoon. MVFR/IFR conditions possible.
Winds out of the NW/WNW at 10-20 kts with gusts of 20-30 kts.

KBOS Terminal...High confidence.

KBDL Terminal...High confidence.

Outlook /Saturday Night through Tuesday/...

Saturday Night: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt.

Sunday through Sunday Night: VFR. Breezy.

Monday: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt.

Monday Night through Tuesday: VFR. Breezy.

will have at least a light -RASN mix 12z-15z Sat which could

Through 00Z...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact
timing.

MVFR for most with spotty IFR. VFR across the Cape/Islands at
the moment, but will see a return to MVFR as showers spread in.
There is a bit of a lull in the strong S winds, but will see
another surge of the low level jet between 20-00Z bringing a
return of 40-50 kt gusts across eastern areas into the evening.
Winds will be shifting to the SW/WSW as a strong cold front
swings through with gusts of 35-45+ kts. Precipitation ending
from west to east mid to late this afternoon and there could be
a touch of snow to wrap things up, but should not accumulate
outside of the higher terrain. There is a lower probability for
western airports (mainly BDL-BAF) where any wet pavement could
freeze and become icy as temperatures plummet heading into this
evening. Further east this risk should be mitigated by the
surge of strong winds, but any spots where there is standing
water could become icy.

MVFR conditions linger with ocean-effect snow showers. Most
likely at ACK, but could leak into HYA/FMH from time to time. Up
to an inch of accumulation is possible at ACK. WSW/SW winds at
15-25 kts with gusts of 35-45 kts in the evening. Gusts ease to
25-35 kts after 06Z.

Saturday and Saturday night...High confidence.

VFR for most, but MVFR/borderline MVFR conditions linger across
the Cape/Islands due to ocean effect snow showers. Will remain
gusty out of the SW/WSW with speeds of 15-20 kts and gusts of
25-35 kts. Winds ease to 5-10 kts Saturday night with gusts of
15-25 kts. The highest gusts confined to the Cape/Islands.
Could see another 1-2 inches of new snow across ACK.

winds become generally SW.

trends.

scattered nature of storms means confidence was too low to
include VCTS in any particular TAF. Mainly IFR to localized
LIFR, though pockets of MVFR possible in the CT River Valley
mid-day.

significant variation in wind direction with E/NE winds across
eastern MA/Cape Cod, and W/SW across the interior. Winds
generally less than 15kt, though gusts to 30 kt possible in
embedded strong thunderstorms.

on trends.

IFR/localized LIFR. Showers begin to wane near 12Z as low
pressure pulls to our east. Winds generally N/NW overnight, less
than 10kt, though may gust to 20kt along the NE MA coastline.

rain and embedded thunderstorms after 05Z through the period.

E/NE winds. Winds gradually shift to the N/NW by daybreak
Sunday.

passes over the terminal this afternoon. Lull in precipitation

thunderstorms develop for Saturday and Saturday night. MVFR to

Forecast Confidence Levels:

06z TAF update:

Through 12z... Moderate confidence. A mixture of LIFR/IFR for
the most, but MVFR on Cape Cod & the Islands along with poor
vsby, between 2-4 SM due to +RA. SE winds continue to gust
between 35-45 kts at coastal terminals, while across the
interior stronger gusts have been hard to achieve, still the
potential is the for SE gusts 25-35 kts. Additionally, there is
60 to 80 knots of wind shear.

Today... High confidence. Conditions improve quickly, west to
east, from LIFR/IFR to MVFR/VFR, between 12z and 15z. Breezy SW
wind 10-20 kts with gust to 30kts.

Tonight... High confidence. VFR, some low end VFR to MVFR
possible across NW MA, decreasing winds out of the SW 10-15 kts.

Thursday... High confidence. VFR, and isolated MVFR CIGS across
high terrain of northern MA. SW wind 10-15 kts.

KBOS TAF... High confidence. A robust storm provides ESE wind
gusts up to 45 kts through 10z/11z, wind shifts to the SW late
morning into early afternoon, with gust between 25/30 kts. CIGS
this morning are IFR, but should see improvements to MVFR
10z-12z, this will coincide with the end of the rainfall before
becoming VFR shortly after.

KBDL TAF... Moderate confidence, low confidence in winds. Wind
forecast has been difficult, have edge the wind gust lower
through 09z, until then ESE wind 10-20 kts possible. Wind shifts
to the SW with increasing wind gust to 25 kts. This coincides
with the end of the rainfall. IFR to MVFR between 09z and 12z,
then becoming VFR 13z to 15z.

Thursday Night through Friday: VFR. Breezy.

Friday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Strong winds with
gusts up to 45 kt. RA, chance SN, isolated TSRA.

up to 50 kt. RA, isolated TSRA.

Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Strong
winds with gusts up to 45 kt.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /09Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

06z TAF Update:

Through 12z Tue: High confidence in trends, but moderate to high
on timing.

IFR-visby snow currently extends from roughly a HFD-PVD-TAN-PYM
line southward with VFR north of this line. Expansion northward
of snow and deteriorating flight categories is expected into
the BDL- CEF- BAF- ORH- BOS line by 08z, then northward towards
BED and points north after 09z. By 12z Tue, expect coatings to
perhaps an inch of snow from the MA/VT/NH border to the Mass
Pike, with better chances at minor accumulation and snow-
covered runways from a couple inches of snow for the BDL-PVD
corridor southward. Transition from -SN to RA may take place
near 12z at HYA and ACK. Light WSW/SW winds initially but will
flip to NE/ENE by 08-10z with speeds around 4-8 kt.

Today: Moderate confidence.

Areas north and west of ORH likely to stay as IFR-visby light
snow; initial IFR-visby light snow elsewhere to transition over
to mixed precip (from SN to PL/FZRA) between 14-18z, and/or to
rain near and southeast of I-95. A period of 1/2SM moderate
intensity snow may develop just before precip-type changeover
and indicated those with TEMPOs. Mainly snowcovered runways at
BAF, with snow- covered to icy runways from a few inches of snow
with a glaze of ice anticipated at BED, ORH, PVD and BDL.
Initial minor snow accumulation at BOS and the Cape airports
likely to be washed away by rain. However by the 20-23z
timeframe as NW winds take over and result in falling temps, a
mixover from rain to PL/FZRA and ending as brief light snow to
take place.

Low pressure passing through I-95 to bring winds from the NE/ENE
for most areas near or west of I-95 with E to ESE winds around
10 kt for the Cape airports to PVD. After 20z, an anticipated
windshift to N and NW are expected with speeds increasing to
around 10-15 kt.

Tonight: High confidence.

Rapid improvement to VFR. Slushy or wet runways may freeze as
temps fall thru the 20s, although NW winds around 10-15 kt with
gusts 25-30 kt may mitigate freeze-up to an extent.

Wednesday: High confidence.

VFR. NW winds 10-15 kt with gusts up to 25 kt.

KBOS TAF...Moderate to high confidence. VFR for another couple
hrs with light snow developing around 08-09z with IFR-visby snow
after 10z. Some accumulation on runways likely, but rising
temps ~15-17z brings snow mixing with and to rain; then ending
as a period of light snow after 21z. Winds become NE around 5-10
kt, then shift to N/NW after 21z with flight categories
improving to VFR after 01z.

KBDL TAF...Moderate to high confidence. VFR-visby light snow to
worsen to IFR by 08z, then remaining as steady light snow. Snow
may become moderate at times by mid morning to early afternoon.
Mainly snow covered runways, though can't rule out minor icing.
NW winds by mid aftn bring decreasing/intermittent light snow,
before improvement to VFR by late-aftn/early evening.

Outlook /Wednesday Night through Saturday/...

Wednesday Night: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt.

Thursday: VFR. Breezy.

Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Breezy.
Slight chance SN.

Friday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Breezy. Chance
SN.

Friday Night: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt. Chance
SN.

Saturday: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt. Slight
chance SN.

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
A weak low pressure trough remains in the vicinity through
Sunday.

Low confidence forecast, especially for tonight, as stratus
spreads/develops westward. Uncertain how far west IFR to LIFR
conditions will be, with higher confidence of the lower
conditions east of the metro terminals. VLIFR is possible at
times at KISP, KBDR and KGON. Also, uncertain with the timing
of lowering conditions, and then improvement Sunday morning.

There is a chance of showers later Sunday morning, becoming
likely during the afternoon. Thunderstorms are possible from the
NYC terminals and north and west mid to late afternoon and into
the early evening. Best chances will be at KSWF and included in
a TEMPO, with a PROB30 at KEWR and KTEB. And there will be a
slight chance of thunder at KLGA, KJFK and KHPN, however, too
low to include in the forecast at this time.

Light S to SE winds become light and variable at most locations
this evening and tonight, and then a southerly flow develops

news.text:
.AVIATION /20Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
A warm front will remain nearby, nearly stationary through the TAF
period.

An area of showers and thunderstorms that developed just south of
the metro terminals will move through between 20-21Z and then move
into the Lower Hudson Valley through 22-23Z. Gusty winds of 40 kt or
higher are possible with these storms, along with hail. However,
given uncertainty where the highest winds will be, kept gusts to 25
kt with these storms.

VFR conditions outside of any showers and thunderstorms this
afternoon. MVFR or lower as fog and low stratus affects the forecast
area once again tonight. Best chances for MVFR is after 00Z-01Z,
then IFR or lower is possible after 03Z. These conditions will occur
a few hours earlier for terminals along the coast.

Outside of thunderstorms, winds will be around 10 kt during the day
today out of the S to SE, weakening to under 10 kt tonight.
Slightly stronger winds of 10 to 15 kt by mid Tuesday morning.

A line of showers and thunderstorms currently pushing northeast of
the metro terminals will move through the Lower Hudson Valley
through around 20Z. Another area of showers and thunderstorms is
currently developing to the southwest over western central and New
Jersey and eastern Pennsylvania will also head northeast this

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A frontal system moves slowly eastward tonight through
Wednesday.

Currently an area of showers and thunderstorms was moving
through northeastern New Jersey, into the NYC metro terminals,
and into the lower Hudson Valley. Conditions mainly VFR with a
chance of MVFR in the showers and thunderstorms. Threat of
thunderstorms ends south soon after 00Z, and by 03Z at KSWF,
and maybe before 02Z. Showers will be possible east of the NYC
metro terminals late evening into late tonight. Scattered
showers are possible overnight, however probabilities too low,
and confidence in areas of showers too uncertain to keep chances
in the TAFs for an extended period of time. The best chances for
thunderstorms Wednesday will be mid to late afternoon, and kept
the PROB30 at this time.

MVFR to IFR stratus is expected to develop once again tonight,
with areal coverage and timing uncertain. However, LIFR is only
expected at KGON late tonight. Conditions rather quickly improve
to VFR Wednesday morning.

Winds S to SE become light and variable at most locations
tonight. The winds then have a more westerly component to them
towards daybreak and increase out of the W SW Wednesday morning.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Thunderstorms have weakened and a rumble/isolate storm remains
possible until around 01Z. There is uncertainty as to how far
west MVFR to IFR stratus will develop late evening, 04Z, and
overnight.

thunderstorms, with MVFR possible, will be ending early in the
evening.

north of the city.

.AVIATION /21Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure approaches from the south, passing east of Long Island
tonight into Sunday.

MVFR cigs/vsbys late today decline to IFR by early evening, then IFR
or lower overnight into Sunday AM. Gradual improvement to MVFR
through Sunday afternoon.

Precipitation is gradually beginning to fall late this afternoon at
city terminals, and will spread east through the remainder of the
day, initially falling as snow, before mixing with and changing to
rain along the coast this evening. Inland terminals remain snow into
tonight, perhaps mixing or changing to rain at KHPN overnight. A
lull in precipitation is expected overnight before a mix of rain and
snow showers redevelops Sunday morning along the coast, with
additional snow showers inland.

E-ENE winds 10-15 kt increase to around 20 kt along the coast
tonight with gusts 25-30 kt here into early Sun AM. Flow lightens
after 12Z Sun, close to 10 kt, as direction backs northerly, then NW.

changes and precipitation onset/ending.

N/NW winds around 10 kt.

afternoon. E winds 15-20kt with gusts 25-30kt in the afternoon. SE

news.text:
.AVIATION /01Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure approaches from the south, passing east of Long Island
tonight into Sunday.

Currently, MVFR to IFR conditions are being reported for most
terminals, except KGON where precipitation has yet to begin.
Conditions will continue to lower to IFR or lower overnight.
Gradual improvement to MVFR through Sunday afternoon, with a
return to VFR around 00Z Monday.

Precipitation will continue to become more widespread over the
next few hours and become more intense. A changeover to rain has

.AVIATION /09Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure departs farther east of the region today into tonight.

Residual low level moisture and intermittent precipitation will keep
IFR conditions through this morning. The precipitation will be more
rain for coastal terminals and more snow for inland terminals.

eastern Great Lakes tonight, sending a strong frontal system across
the area. This will be a high impact event with strong winds and
heavy rains.

rainfall and winds increase across the terminals. Brief LIFR is
possible. Confidence on fog development remains low.

highest at the coastal terminals. Highest winds will be after 00Z
and up until the cold frontal passage, which will be from west to
east from approximately 09Z to 12Z. Post-frontal WSW winds will
gusts 30-35kt, possibly a few higher gusts, especially Wednesday
afternoon. There could be a lull in the winds briefly as the front
moves through.

An isolated thunderstorms is possible overnight.

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

.AVIATION /03Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
***Major Storm System to Impact Terminals Through Tonight***

Deepening low pressure over the Midwest tracks into the Eastern
Great Lakes tonight, sending a strong frontal system across the
area. This is a high impact event with strong winds and heavy rains
now taking place.

Brief LIFR is possible at a few terminals for a few hours, but will
not be the rule, but rather the exception. Otherwise IFR prevails at
most terminals.

SE winds have ramped up reaching 25-30 G45-50kt late this evening,
with the highest at the coastal terminals. These high winds will
take place until the cold frontal passage, which will be from west
to east from approximately 08Z to 11Z. There could be a brief lull
in the winds as the front moves through. Post-frontal WSW winds on
Wednesday 15-22G30-35kt, with possibly a few higher gusts,
especially for the afternoon.

A few isolated thunderstorms remain possible over the next several
hours, mainly for eastern terminals.

...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

for higher gusts is at KJFK.

could end as a brief period of snow or mix.

into evening before another round of rain moves in late tonight

afternoon into the start of this evening, generally 20Z to 00Z.

differences and spatial differences in categories that could
vary a few hours from forecast, the forecast has low confidence.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...

Forecaster Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Medium - 30 to 60 percent. High -
greater than 60 percent.

00Z TAF update...

Tonight...High Confidence in trends but moderate confidence in
timing.

IFR conditions continue for the first half of the
evening in snow which was reducing vsbys to generally 1 or 2
miles. We should see improvement to MVFR conditions from
northeast to southwest roughly in the 2z to 6z timeframe...but
perhaps an hour or two later across portions of CT and areas
near the south coast. This a result of drier air working in
from the north allowing the steady snow to taper off to more
scattered light snow showers/flurries. Ptype will be all snow
pretty much northwest of the Cape Cod Canal. A general 1 to 4
inches of snow is expected on untreated runways with the higher
amounts across our western terminals. N winds 5-15 knots.

Tomorrow...High Confidence

Lingering MVFR ceilings should improve to VFR by
lunchtime...except for the far southeast New England coast where
this process may take a bit longer. There may also be lingering
ocean enhanced scattered light rain/snow showers in the
morning. Otherwise...NNW winds 10 to 15 knots with a few gusts
near 25 knots along the coast.

Tomorrow Night...High Confidence

VFR. Northwest winds 5 to 10 knots.

KBOS Terminal...High Confidence in trends but moderate confidence in
timing.

KBDL Terminal...High Confidence in trends but moderate confidence in
timing.

Outlook /Tuesday through Friday/...

Tuesday: VFR. Breezy.

Tuesday Night: VFR. Windy with gusts up to 30 kt.

Wednesday through Wednesday Night: VFR. Windy with gusts up to
35 kt.

Thursday: VFR. Breezy.

Thursday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Windy with local
gusts up to 30 kt. Chance RA, chance SN.

Friday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Strong winds with
local gusts up to 40 kt. RA.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /21Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
18z TAF Update:

Rest of the Afternoon (thru 00z Fri): Moderate confidence.

Mix of VFR-MVFR ceilings thru 21z. Conditions then trend more
solidly sub-VFR after 21z to 00z west of ORH. Light NE winds in
the interior to gradually become E/ESE; eastern/coastal MA,
mainly E winds eastern MA/RI and ESE winds Cape and Islands.
Speeds in all areas generally less than 10 kt.

Tonight: High confidence in trends, moderate on timing.

Deterioration all sites this period with MVFR-IFR ceilings,
advancing precip (largely -RA/RA, but higher elev -SN thru 06z in
the Berkshires and northern hills in Worcester County), and
increased E/SE gusts.

Winds increase to become ESE sustained 15-25 kt/gusts 35-45 kt
with areas of low-level shear/turbulence.

Friday: High confidence in trends, moderate on timing.

**Significant aviation impacts probable this period.**

Through the morning...IFR-possible LIFR ceilings with VFR/MVFR
with steady rain, some heavy at times (low prob T/TS
eastern/southeast airports 12-16z). Strong SE winds, gusts 40-50
kt strongest eastern/southeast MA and the Cape. Areas of LLWS
still possible.

After 16z...a powerful cold front then moves through the TAFs
with a rapid decrease in rain covg, ceilings improving to MVFR-
VFR levels and a gusty wind shift from SE to SW/WSW, gusts 35-45
kt. Lower probability for the western airports (mainly BDL-BAF)
that any wet pavement could freeze and become icy as
temperatures fall into the upper 20s between 21-00z Sat.

Friday Night: High confidence.

MVFR to VFR with gusty W to SW winds gusts up to 45 kt.
Generally dry but ocean effect SHSN possible at ACK and perhaps
HYA/FMA. Rapid temperature fall likely Fri night that may cause
icy spots on runways.

KBOS Terminal...Moderate confidence.

KBDL Terminal...Moderate confidence.

Outlook /Saturday through Tuesday/...

Saturday: VFR. Windy with gusts up to 35 kt. Slight chance SN.

Saturday Night: VFR. Windy with gusts up to 35 kt.

Christmas Day: VFR. Windy with areas of gusts up to 30 kt.

Sunday Night through Monday: VFR. Breezy.

Monday Night through Tuesday: VFR.

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
12z TAFs: Moderate confidence.

IFR/MVFR this morning in rain and fog. Strong SE winds gusting
to 40-50kt with LLWS given 50-60+ kt winds around 2000 ft.

rapid decrease in rain coverage, ceilings improving to MVFR or
lower-end VFR, and a wind shift from S to SW/WSW with gusts

temperatures fall into the upper 20s between 21-00z Sat.

possible at ACK and perhaps HYA/FMH. Rapid temperature fall

temperatures continue Saturday.

18z TAF update:

Thru 00z...moderate confidence, some uncertainty on south and
eastward extent of thunderstorms.

VFR for most terminals. VFR cloud bases and vsbys in -TSRA
across the high terrain of MA/CT. These storms may traverse into
the coastal plain, but likely with less intensity than current
state. Stronger storms inland may contain gusty winds, small
hail and brief heavy downpours. Stratus/fog over ACK should
remain LIFR cigs but VFR vsbys, but then lower to IFR/LIFR
toward and especially after 00z.

Tonight...Moderate confidence.

Deteriorating cigs to IFR from E to W as backdoor front moves
through. Scattered t-storms early, otherwise scattered showers
persisting through the night, greatest coverage in eastern New
Eng. Increasing NE winds overnight with gusts to 25 kt
developing along the coast and 15-20 kt elsewhere.

Saturday...Moderate confidence.

MVFR/IFR conditions in the morning with scattered showers, then
gradually improving to VFR in the afternoon, especially
interior. MVFR persisting across SE New Eng. NE gusts to 25 kt
BOS-PVD corridor and up to 30 kt Cape/Islands.

Saturday night...moderate confidence.

MVFR across southeast MA with low risk of showers. NE winds
15-25 kt becoming north 15-20 KT. Elsewhere, VFR with gusty NE
winds slackening and becoming north.

surrounding if convection makes it to the terminal and at what

between 00Z-03Z

isolated TSRA.

news.text:
.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 12Z...High confidence in trends, low confidence in
exact timing.

Widespread IFR with LIFR across eastern MA and RI. Limited
shower activity left for the rest of the morning, mainly for
terminals on Cape Cod and the islands in the next few hours.
Risk of thunder is low but not zero, mainly over Cape Cod and
the islands. Winds out of the E/SE 5-10 kts.

Today after 12Z...Moderate confidence.

Conditions will be slow to improve from IFR/LIFR to VFR/MVFR.
Anticipating that western terminals become VFR by the afternoon,
but eastern areas may only see several hours of MVFR cigs/vsbys
return after around 21Z. Can't rule out a spot shower across
the interior during the afternoon. Winds light and variable
across the interior and south coast. Northeastern MA will see E
to northeast winds around 5kts.

Tonight...Moderate confidence.

VFR across western terminals improving to VFR across the south
coast. Elsewhere will see conditions lowering to MVFR with
perhaps some patchy fog and a spot shower or two. Winds light
and variable.

Wednesday...High confidence.

VFR. Scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon
and evening, some of which could be strong to severe. Southerly
winds 5 to 10 kts.

KBOS Terminal...High confidence in TAF trends, but moderate on
exact timing. With onshore flow expecting conditions to remain
LIFR for the AM push. Will be slow to improve with onshore
flow. May get to low end MVFR by 18Z.

KBDL Terminal...High confidence in TAF.

Wednesday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance

06z TAF Update:

Through 12z Tue: High confidence in trends, but moderate to high

IFR-visby snow currently extends from roughly a HFD-PVD-TAN-PYM
line southward with VFR north of this line. Expansion northward
of snow and deteriorating flight categories is expected into
the BDL- CEF- BAF- ORH- BOS line by 08z, then northward towards
BED and points north after 09z. By 12z Tue, expect coatings to
perhaps an inch of snow from the MA/VT/NH border to the Mass
Pike, with better chances at minor accumulation from snow-
covered runways from a couple inches of snow for the BDL-PVD
corridor southward. Transition from -SN to RA may take place
near 12z at HYA and ACK. Light WSW/SW winds initially but will
flip to NE/ENE by 08-10z with speeds around 4-8 kt.

Today: Moderate confidence.

Areas north and west of ORH likely to stay as IFR-visby light
snow; initial IFR-visby light snow elsewhere to transition over
to mixed precip (from SN to PL/FZRA) between 14-18z, and/or to
rain near and southeast of I-95. A period of 1/2SM moderate
intensity snow may develop just before precip-type changeover
and indicated those with TEMPOs. Mainly snowcovered runways at
BAF, with snow- covered to icy runways from a few inches of snow
with a glaze of ice anticipated at BED, ORH, PVD and BDL.
Initial minor snow accumulation at BOS and the Cape airports
likely to be washed away by rain. However by the 20-23z
timeframe as NW winds take over and result in falling temps, a
mixover from rain to PL/FZRA and ending as brief light snow to
take place.

Low pressure passing through I-95 to bring winds from the NE/ENE
for most areas near or west of I-95 with E to ESE winds around
10 kt for the Cape airports to PVD. After 20z, an anticipated
windshift to N and NW are expected with speeds increasing to
around 10-15 kt.

Tonight: High confidence.

temps fall thru the 20s, although NW winds around 10-15 kt with
gusts 25-30 kt may mitigate freeze-up to an extent.

after 10z. Some accumulation on runways likely, but rising

as a period of light snow after 21z. Winds become NE around 5-10
kt, then shift to N/NW after 21z with flight categories

news.text:
.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
A cold front will move through this evening followed by high
pressure building in tonight into Thursday.

Mainly LIFR to IFR currently, with slight improvements to IFR
expected around 20-21z. There is then a chance that IFR could
hang on longer than forecast if the cold front passage ends up a
bit slower than currently anticipated. Have showed this with a
TEMPO group around the NYC terminals from 00z-02z. VFR conditions
should return quickly tonight behind the cold front. The bulk of
the rainfall is now across eastern areas, with lingering light
showers and -DZ.

S-SSW winds generally around 10 kt or less this afternoon with
some locations variable at times as the flow lightens. Winds
veer to the SW-W towards evening from NYC metro terminals on NW,
and after 00z across Long Island and S CT. Increasing NW flow
occurs overnight into Thursday morning as the cold front moves
offshore. Gusts around 20-22 KT expected on Thursday.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
Thinking the 1/4 SM FG at JFK will hang on the next hour or so
and eventually improve slightly as winds become more westerly.

Amendments likely for changing visibilities/ceilings this
afternoon.

There is a chance that LIFR continues to linger longer than
previous forecast. There is also a chance that IFR continues
longer than currently forecast this evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY...
.Thursday...VFR. NW gusts around 20kt.
.Friday-Saturday...Mainly VFR. NE gusts 15-20kt possible on
Saturday
.Sunday...VFR to start, then chance of rain with MVFR conditions,
possibly mixed with snow inland. N-NE winds G20kt.
.Monday...Lingering MVFR possible in the morning, then VFR with
N wind.

news.text:
.AVIATION /22Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
High Impact Aviation Event to Unfold this evening into Friday.

A warm frontal wave approaches from the south through tonight,
passing through Friday morning. This will be followed by an arctic
cold frontal passage Friday afternoon.

E winds will ramp up through tonight, increasing to 15-20kt
G30kt for the evening push. E-SE LLWS developing after 00Z,
increasing to 50 to 60 kt at 2kft toward 09Z. Winds will then
veer to the SE 06Z to 09Z as the warm front approaches, with the
gust potential increasing to 35 to 40 kt. However, gusts may be
more occasional than frequent until the warm front passes
around 12Z Friday. The best potential for frequent G40kt will
come after the cold frontal passage 17-19Z, with WSW
20-30G35-45kt.

Ceilings will lower to IFR into this evening. Improvement to
MVFR following the warm frontal passage Friday morning and
eventually VFR in the afternoon behind the arctic cold front.

Conditions may dry out Friday morning for a couple of hours. A
line of moderate to heavy showers will then be possible along
and ahead of the arctic cold front, with the potential for snow
mixing in, especially NW of the city terminals. Temperatures
will abruptly fall behind the cold front (more than 10 degrees
in an hour), reaching freezing within 1 to 2 hours following its
passage.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments likely though the TAF period for changing cigs/vsbys
and onset of gusts. Timing of onset of gusts 30-35kt for the PM
push with conds deteriorating to IFR conds in RA could be +/-
an hour off. LLWS likely at all terminals after 00Z, though
could be an hour or two later than currently forecast.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY...
.Friday Afternoon...Becoming VFR. WSW winds 20-30G35-45kt,
gradually subsiding Friday night.
.Saturday...VFR. WSW winds 15-20G20-30 kt, diminishing in the
afternoon.
.Sunday....VFR. W winds 10-15G20kt.
.Monday and Tuesday...VFR.

news.text:
.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A backdoor cold front approaches this afternoon and passes
through overnight. High pressure builds towards the region out
of southeast Canada on Saturday.

VFR through this early evening. There is a chance for showers
and thunderstorms, mainly inland across Lower Hudson Valley and
Connecticut into early this evening. The probability of
thunderstorms increases towards 00z and continues into the first
half of the night closer to the coast. The chance for thunder
diminishes after 03/04z, but showers remain likely into the
early morning hours. Brief MVFR is possible in heavier
downpours.

MVFR ceilings should become widespread from north to south
after 06z. IFR becomes likely early Saturday morning,
transitioning to MVFR by middle morning and then VFR in the
afternoon.

S-SE flow around 10 kt this afternoon with some inland
terminals remaining NE. Winds should start backing towards the
ESE-E this evening, becoming variable the first half of tonight.
Winds will become NE and increase early Saturday morning once
the backdoor front moves south of the area. Sustained NE winds
around 15 kt with gusts 20-25 kt likely on Saturday.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of thunderstorms may need to be adjusted this evening.

Timing of wind shift to the NE late tonight may be off by 1-2 hours.

OUTLOOK FOR 18Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

Saturday PM: Becoming VFR. Becoming VFR in the afternoon. NE winds
around 15kt with gusts around 25kt, highest at the coastal
terminals. Winds diminishing in the evening.

Sunday: Mostly VFR, a chance of MVFR with showers east of the NYC
metro terminals. NE wind gusts 15-20 kt possible.

Monday: VFR, a slight chance of showers.

Tuesday-Wednesday: Mainly VFR, a chance of mainly afternoon and
evening showers and thunderstorms with MVFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

overnight. High pressure builds towards the region out of southeast

transitioning to MVFR by middle morning and then VFR in the
afternoon.

Winds should start backing towards the ESE-E this evening,
becoming variable the first half of tonight. Winds will become
NE and increase early Saturday morning once the backdoor front
moves south of the area. Sustained NE winds around 15 kt with
gusts 20-25 kt likely on Saturday.

news.speaker: NWS New York forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /20Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Low pressure centered over the eastern Great Lakes has a warm front
in the vicinity of Long Island. The warm front may move farther
north as a cold front approaches to the west. The cold front, with a
wave of low pressure, then moves across the terminals this evening
into tonight. Weak low pressure remains to the north Tuesday.

Stratus moved into the coastal terminals with MVFR conditions, and
IFR possible at times. Delayed onset of showers an hour or so, as
showers will be more likely early this evening, with IFR conditions.
Timing of lowering to IFR is uncertain, with the coastal terminals
lowering first. Thunderstorms will be possible this evening with a
few possibly having gusting winds, especially inland. Ceilings may
improve to MVFR with the cold front passage, however, at this time
IFR looks to be most likely. Also, winds may become briefly gusty
with the cold front.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

morning. A weak low pressure trough will then linger over
western portions of the Tri-State area through the weekend.

confidence.

afternoon hours, with MVFR possible some time after 18Z.

to scattered in nature to the east.

Low pressure approaches from the west, impacting the terminals
tonight into Saturday.

VFR early this evening, MVFR cigs quickly develop around 03Z
Saturday as rain moves in. IFR or lower tonight into Saturday
morning. PROB30 remains for thunderstorms late tonight.

SE flow around 10 kt increases toward 03Z Sat 20-25 kt with
gusts over 30 kt. Gusts may be as high as 45 kt for a period
05Z to 10Z, especially along the coast. LLWS develops around 05Z
through 12Z with 2kft winds up to 65 kt. Winds become SW
Saturday morning. Winds lighten under 20 kt for a period Sat AM,
increasing again late morning into the afternoon, gusts to
mainly 30-35 kt, with potential for an isolated 40 kt gust.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

categories.

terminals through tonight.

or early this afternoon.

forecast. Brief G35-40kt possible this afternoon.

.AVIATION /20Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure will be northeast of the region with an arctic cold
front approaching Sunday.

Mainly VFR conditions are forecast through the TAF period. Exception
will be Sunday afternoon with potential for snow showers as well as
snow squalls. These could present a brief period of IFR or lower
conditions.

Gusty winds will prevail through the TAF period. Wind direction
westerly going into tonight, becoming more SW on Sunday. Sustained
wind speeds near 20-25 kt through this evening and then 15-20 kt
late tonight into Sunday morning, before returning back to near 20-
25 kt Sunday afternoon. Gusts near 30-35 kt going into this evening,
then closer to 25-30 kt late tonight into Sunday morning. Sunday
afternoon, gusts rise back to near 35 kt.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Peak gusts to near 40 kt possible at times, especially Sunday
afternoon.

OUTLOOK FOR 21Z SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

Late Sunday afternoon into Sunday night: VFR returning. W wind
gusts 35-40 kt into early evening, then decreasing to near
20-25 kt mid to late evening and thereafter.

Monday: Mainly VFR. IFR possible with chance of light snow late
Monday night.

Tuesday: IFR and snow likely. Snow tapers off at night. VFR
eventually returns.

Wednesday: VFR. W wind gusts near 20-25kt.

Thursday: VFR. WSW gusts up to near 20 kt.

news.text:
.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Low pressure slowly lifts north of New England tonight. An arctic
cold front approaches Sunday morning and moves through Sunday
afternoon and early evening.

Gusty WSW-SW winds will continue tonight. Sustained speeds around 20
kt with gusts 30-35 kt will continue through 02z before slowly
weakening into the early morning hours. Gusts should end up
closer to 20-25 kt around day break and some outlying terminals
could see the gusts briefly end. SW flow increases through
Sunday morning ahead of the arctic front with sustained speeds
20-25 kt in the afternoon gusting 30-35 kt.

Mainly VFR conditions through the TAF period with the only exception
of potential for brief IFR or lower in snow showers or snow squalls
with the arctic cold front. Gusts 35-40 kt may accompany the fropa.

Winds shift to the W-WNW with potential for gusts around 35-40kt
late afternoon into early evening.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
A few peak gusts around 35-40 kt possible through 02z.

Gusts could become occasional 09-14z.

Peak gusts 40-45 kt possible at times Sunday afternoon and
evening.

OUTLOOK FOR 00Z MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY...

Sunday night: VFR. W-WNW wind gusts 35-40 kt early, then decreasing
to near 20-25 kt mid to late evening. Gusts likely end after 04z.

Monday: VFR.

Monday Night-Tuesday. MVFR or lower possible with light snow late
Monday Night. IFR or lower with light snow on Tuesday, tapering off
in the evening.

Wednesday-Thursday: VFR. W wind gusts near 20-25kt on Wednesday.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

An Arctic cold front will approach this morning and move across
this afternoon. High pressure will then build in from the west
tonight.

Gusty WSW-SW winds will continue early this morning, with gusts
generally around 25 kt, but still potential for some gusts over
30 kt (KLGA brief G35kt right at 06Z but has since diminished).
Winds should briefly diminish toward daybreak, with gusts
possibly ending or becoming occasional at some outlying
terminals. SW flow after 13Z-14Z ahead of the Arctic front
increases to 20-25 kt by this afternoon, gusting to 30-35 kt.

Winds shift to the W-WNW with the fropa, with gusts 35-40 kt
possible late this afternoon and early this evening. Winds will
then slowly weaken through tonight.

There is potential for brief IFR or lower cond in snow showers
or squalls with the Arctic cold front.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Gusts could briefly become occasional from about 10Z-13Z.

Timing of -SHSN may be off by 1-3 hours.

cold fropa this afternoon and early this evening.
